treatment.schedule_summary: Dacarbazine 850 mg/m² IV on day 1 every 21 days for 6 cycles or until progression or unacceptable toxicity, whichever occurs first.
treatment.duration_text: 6 cycles or until progression/toxicity, whichever occurs first
administration_instructions: Dacarbazine 850 mg/m² IV on day 1 every 21 days, for up to 6 cycles or earlier progression/unacceptable toxicity.
Use 1000 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over 1 hour under NCCP 00464. Protect solution and infusion set from light.
Antiemetics follow the high-risk NCCP/local supportive-care plan. Do not interpret “no routine premedications” as omitting antiemetics.

components.note: 1000 mL sodium chloride 0.9%; protect solution and infusion set from light.

Current HPRA SmPC differs for isolated mild/moderate impairment; no calculated dose or automatic permission to treat.

action.message: Preserve the documented individualized dose history. Table 1 recovery to 100% must not silently reverse an existing renal/hepatic or toxicity reduction; the consultant/pharmacist must confirm the restart dose.

action.message: Symptoms of a hypersensitivity reaction require immediate cessation of dacarbazine and urgent clinical assessment. This applies before a severe grade is reached; do not automatically rechallenge.

action.message: Hepatic veno-occlusive disease during dacarbazine makes further therapy contraindicated. Do not rechallenge simply because current liver tests have recovered.

action.message: Stop the dacarbazine infusion immediately and follow the local extravasation protocol. Extravasation can cause severe pain and tissue damage. Any remaining dose requires team assessment and a different vein; do not automatically resume.

source.document: HPRA Dacarbazine medac 200 mg SmPC, March 2024

action.message: Avoid concomitant phenytoin because reduced gastrointestinal absorption may exacerbate convulsions. Reconcile the antiseizure plan with oncology/pharmacy before treatment.

action.message: Avoid live vaccines during dacarbazine. SmPC permits consideration no sooner than 3 months after chemotherapy and only after immune-status review. Review any recent exposure or proposed vaccination; this is not a general vaccination schedule.

source.document: HPRA Dacarbazine medac 200 mg SmPC, March 2024

action.message: For an anticoagulant monitored by INR, increase INR monitoring as clinically appropriate because cancer and treatment can cause variable interactions. This does not imply INR monitoring for direct oral anticoagulants.

action.message: Current HPRA SmPC: effective contraception during treatment and for 6 months afterwards for women and 3 months afterwards for men. Discuss fertility preservation before treatment and genetic counselling where relevant. The archived NCCP-linked 100 mg SmPC has outdated male timing.

source.document: HPRA Dacarbazine medac 200 mg SmPC, March 2024

action.message: Urgently assess infection, bleeding or suspected marrow toxicity before further dacarbazine. Delayed cumulative myelosuppression can occur, with white-cell/platelet nadirs often at 3–4 weeks; a simple day7–14 safe/unsafe calendar is not supported.

source.document: HPRA Dacarbazine medac 200 mg SmPC, March 2024

rules.explanation: Urgently assess infection, bleeding or suspected marrow toxicity before further dacarbazine. Delayed cumulative myelosuppression can occur, with white-cell/platelet nadirs often at 3–4 weeks; a simple day7–14 safe/unsafe calendar is not supported.

action.message: Assess persistent vomiting, poor intake or dehydration promptly and optimize prescribed antiemetics, hydration and electrolytes. Dacarbazine is high emetogenic risk; no routine premedication does not mean no antiemetics.

rules.explanation: Assess persistent vomiting, poor intake or dehydration promptly and optimize prescribed antiemetics, hydration and electrolytes. Dacarbazine is high emetogenic risk; no routine premedication does not mean no antiemetics.

action.message: Review previous febrile neutropenia or prolonged marrow toxicity and the documented dose/support plan. Dacarbazine myelosuppression can be cumulative; NCCP supplies no automatic percentage reduction or universal G-CSF rule for this history.

source.document: HPRA Dacarbazine medac 200 mg SmPC, March 2024

rules.explanation: Review previous febrile neutropenia or prolonged marrow toxicity and the documented dose/support plan. Dacarbazine myelosuppression can be cumulative; NCCP supplies no automatic percentage reduction or universal G-CSF rule for this history.

action.message: Cyclosporine or tacrolimus may cause excessive immunosuppression and risk of lymphoproliferation with dacarbazine. Obtain specialist medication review.

source.document: HPRA Dacarbazine medac 200 mg SmPC, March 2024

rules.explanation: Cyclosporine or tacrolimus may cause excessive immunosuppression and risk of lymphoproliferation with dacarbazine. Obtain specialist medication review.

action.message: Concomitant methoxypsoralen can enhance photosensitization. Review medicines and appropriate sun protection with the team.

source.document: HPRA Dacarbazine medac 200 mg SmPC, March 2024

eligibility: Metastatic malignant melanoma; treatment initiated and supervised by an oncology specialist.
FBC, renal and liver profile at baseline and before each cycle; assess current symptoms and previous doses.
The NCCP document specifies no numeric ECOG or molecular selection threshold for this regimen.
exclusions: Leukopenia and/or thrombocytopenia; Table 1 provides ANC/platelet treatment-delay thresholds

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Highest emetogenic active component and current NCCP classification.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for high emetogenic risk
supportive_care.source_note: NCCP p2 high emetogenic risk; p3 no routine additional premedication. Use the separate high-risk antiemetic plan; clinical/pharmacy review remains pending.

baseline: Assess pregnancy/breastfeeding, contraception/fertility, hypersensitivity, medicines and severe organ disease
during: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle
Monitor for cumulative delayed marrow toxicity, infection/bleeding, nausea/vomiting, hydration, hepatic/renal symptoms and infusion-site injury
Confirm planned cycle number, progression, toxicity and prior reductions at each review
after: Report delayed infection, bleeding, new liver/renal symptoms or other serious effects after the last dose. Follow the individualized post-treatment plan.
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Disease assessment, scans and any additional tests follow the consultant treatment plan; no universal imaging interval or routine tumour-marker panel is specified.
